hero: In the emergency room of a provincial hospital in Laguna at night, a Filipino internal medicine resident and an intern compare three blood gas printouts on a counter while three Filipino men lie on nearby stretchers, one breathing deeply; in the background a nephrology fellow speaks on a phone beside a hemodialysis machine being primed; focused, urgent mood, no text.

figures.teaches: A fixed stepwise reading of the blood gas moves from pH to primary process to compensation to gaps to cause.
figures.content: Vertical flowchart. Box 1 'pH: <7.35 acidemia, >7.45 alkalemia (call if <7.2)'. Box 2 'Primary process: HCO3 or PaCO2?' with four outcomes. Box 3 for metabolic acidosis: 'Expected PaCO2 = 1.5 x HCO3 + 8 (±2) (Albert, Dell, Winters 1967); higher = added respiratory acidosis; lower = added respiratory alkalosis'. Box 4 'Anion gap = Na - (Cl + HCO3); add 2.5 per 1 g/dL albumin below normal (Figge 1998)'. Branch HIGH: 'Ketones (DKA), lactate, kidney failure, toxins'; sub-box 'Osmolal gap = measured - (2 Na + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8); high early in toxic alcohol'; note 'Delta ratio: prompt only, varies widely'. Branch NORMAL: 'Gut or kidney bicarbonate loss, chloride gain'; sub-box 'Urine anion gap = Na + K - Cl: negative = gut loss; positive = kidney (RTA)'. Bottom box: 'Does it fit the story?'.

figures.teaches: The anion gap shows whether lost bicarbonate was replaced by an unmeasured anion or by chloride, and in methanol poisoning the osmolal and anion gaps move in opposite directions over time.
figures.content: Three Gamblegram pairs of stacked columns (cations left: sodium plus potassium; anions right: chloride, bicarbonate, unmeasured anions). Panel 1 'Normal': bicarbonate 24, gap about 12 (mainly albumin). Panel 2 'High-gap acidosis (methanol case)': sodium 138, chloride 100, bicarbonate 5, unmeasured anions enlarged to gap 33, labeled 'formate'. Panel 3 'Normal-gap acidosis': bicarbonate small, chloride enlarged, gap unchanged, labeled 'diarrhea or RTA'. Inset line graph over 0 to 48 hours after methanol ingestion: 'Osmolal gap' line falling, 'Anion gap' line rising, crossing; note 'Ethanol co-ingestion delays the crossing'. Footer: 'EXTRIP: dialysis for coma, seizures, new vision deficits, pH ≤7.15, persistent acidosis, anion gap >24 mmol/L, high methanol level or impaired kidney function'.

card: Three blood gas printouts on an emergency room counter beside a bottle-shaped silhouette, no text.
